claims.quote: `string/chars` splits a string into its Unicode characters in order, keeping astral characters whole: `["string/chars", "a𝄞b"]` gives `["a", "𝄞", "b"]`.

`array/filter` keeps items of a list for which a boolean predicate gives `true`, in plain code, waiting rules, and the symbolic solver: `["array/filter", ["array/make", 1, 5, 2], ["lambda", ["x"], ["number/greaterThan", "x", 2]]]` gives `[5]`.
`array/reverse` reverses a list in plain code, waiting rules, and the symbolic solver: `["array/reverse", ["array/make", 1, 2, 3]]` gives `[3, 2, 1]`.

`array/sort` sorts a list in ascending canonical order or stably by an optional two-argument boolean comparator, in plain code, waiting rules, and the symbolic solver: `["array/sort", ["array/make", 3, 1, 2]]` gives `[1, 2, 3]`.
